ORIGINAL: spinner.dart's doc comment describes and reproduces an OLDER, already-fixed web bug: 'spinner.tsx hands Icon a role="status" and an aria-label="Loading", and Icon... spreads nothing — so both attributes, and data-slot, are dropped on the floor... The spinner announces nothing.' The Dart file explicitly chooses to reproduce that silence under 'ruling B9.' But the CURRENT components/ui/spinner.tsx (read directly) has already been rewritten to host role/aria-label/sr-only text on an outer <span> specifically to fix this — it is not a bare Icon anymore. So the Flutter port is now stale: it reproduces a defect the web has since corrected, and Spinner (Flutter) still renders no status host and no announced text at all, via ExcludeSemantics wrapping the whole thing unconditionally.

api.flutter: Spinner({size = Spinner.px (16), strokeOverride}) — size sets the rendered box, strokeOverride independently overrides the stroke width which is otherwise fixed at Icon.strokeFor(Spinner.px) regardless of size.
api.web: Spinner({className, aria-label, aria-hidden, ...props}) sizes via the caller's className (default size-4 = 16px) exactly as spinner.dart's px constant documents, with the same 'stroke does not scale with a larger className' behavior implicit in using a fixed Loader2Icon glyph.

states.flutter: _SpinnerState drives a single continuous AnimationController.repeat() at MotionDurations.spin, with reduced-motion collapsing it to one held frame at controller.lowerBound (upright, 0°) rather than stopping animation entirely — 'stops the controller at its lower bound... 0°, upright, still.'
states.web: spinner.tsx's anim-spin utility is pulls-spin 0.9s linear infinite per the doc comment, and the file explicitly notes 'linear on purpose... a spinner that eases is a spinner that looks like it is struggling' — the only animation in the system with no --ease-* curve, matching Flutter's MotionCurves usage bypass (RotationTransition has no curve applied, turns runs linearly with the controller).

disabled.flutter: Spinner has no enabled/disabled field — it is a pure loading indicator with a fixed animation.
disabled.web: spinner.tsx defines no disabled prop; the spinner's only conditional behavior is aria-hidden vs role=status based on the decorative flag.
disabled.note: A spinner represents an in-progress state, not a control; there is nothing to disable on either platform.

interaction.flutter: Spinner wires no GestureDetector, Focus, or key handling — it is decoration inside whatever control hosts it (e.g. a loading Button).
interaction.web: spinner.tsx renders a <span> with no onClick, tabIndex, or keyboard handling.
interaction.note: Neither implementation is itself operable; a spinner communicates state, it does not receive input.

semantics.flutter: Spinner.build() always wraps its content in ExcludeSemantics unconditionally, with the doc comment stating 'the glyph is wrapped in ExcludeSemantics... and Button carries the busy state alone' — there is no label parameter, no role='status' equivalent, and no way for a Flutter caller to opt the spinner itself into announcing anything.
semantics.web: The current spinner.tsx computes `const decorative = ariaHidden === true || ariaHidden === 'true'` and, when NOT decorative, renders role='status' aria-label={label ?? 'Loading'} plus a visible-to-AT sr-only text node — so by default (no aria-hidden passed) a web Spinner DOES announce 'Loading' via a live region, and only opts out when the caller explicitly passes aria-hidden.
